01
Logo

One mark, four lockups

The logo pairs a globe arc with the GSS monogram. The gold arc stands for reach; the blue meridians for the network of people we place. Always use the supplied artwork files and never redraw the logo.

Primary (stacked)

The default. Use wherever space is roughly square: profiles, signage, cover pages.

logo-square.svg

Horizontal

For wide, short spaces: website headers, email signatures, letterheads.

icon landscape.svg

Icon

The monogram alone. For app icons, favicons, social avatars and small spaces.

icon only.svg

Wordmark

The name only. Use when the icon already appears nearby on the same surface.

textonly.svg

Colour versions

Full colour

On white or Mist backgrounds. First choice.

White (reversed)

On Navy, Blue or dark photography.

White on Blue

For accent panels and social graphics.

Black

Single-colour printing, stamps, fax and newsprint only.

xxxx

Clear space and minimum size

x

Clear space

Keep an empty margin of x on every side, where x is ¼ of the logo’s height. No text, edges or other graphics inside it.

↧

Minimum size

Below these sizes the tagline and meridians blur. Switch to the icon instead.

Primary64px · 20mm tall
Horizontal32px · 10mm tall
Icon24px · 8mm tall

Logo misuse

Stretch or squash

Always scale proportionally.

Rotate or tilt

The logo always sits level.

Recolour

Use only the four approved versions.

Add effects

No shadows, glows, bevels or outlines.

Busy backgrounds

Place it on a flat brand colour or a calm photo area.

Colour logo on dark

Navy type disappears. Use the white version.

03
Typography

Poppins, everywhere

Poppins is a geometric sans-serif that echoes the round letterforms in the GSS monogram. One family covers headlines, body copy and labels. It is free on Google Fonts.

04
Grid & spacing

Everything on 8

Sizes, spacing, line heights and layout columns are all multiples of 8 pixels. Use 4px only for very tight details like icon padding. This keeps layouts consistent across web, print and slides.

Card on the grid24px padding · 8px gap
Fine line every 8px · strong line every 64px

Layout columns

Desktop · 1440px12 columns · 24px gutter · 80px margin
Tablet · 768px8 col · 16px gutter · 32px margin
Mobile · 390px4 col · 16px gutter · 16px margin

For print, use the same idea in millimetres: A4 pages use a 12-column grid with 5mm gutters and 20mm margins; calling cards (90 × 54mm) keep 4mm safe margins.

05
Graphic elements

Slants and hexagons

Two supporting graphics give GSS layouts their look. Slanted bands suggest forward movement; a faint hexagon pattern suggests a connected network. Use one or both, never so much that they compete with the content.

Slanted bands

Stack 2–3 parallelograms in Navy, Blue and Ice (#C9D7EF), all leaning the same way. Bleed them off a corner or edge. Add one thin Gold slant as the accent.

Hexagon pattern

A light line pattern at 5–10% strength behind content. Use on white (light grey lines) or Navy (white lines). Never behind small body text.

Keep angles consistent

All slants lean the same direction on a page.

Leave space for content

Shapes sit at corners and edges, not under text.

Add gradients or new colours

Shapes use flat brand colours only.

06
Applications

The system in use

The calling card brings everything together: logo on white, Navy and Blue slants, a Gold accent, Poppins type and an 8pt rhythm. The same rules carry over to the presentation and document templates.
